approved: Australian Postal Corporation and Other Legislation Amendment Bill 2024
Infrastructure, Transport, Regional Development, Communications and the Arts
Written by a model from the explanatory memorandum; not the record
This bill updates Australia's rules for screening and inspecting international mail at the border.
The changes start on a date set by Proclamation, or six months after Royal Assent if no date is set.
The distinction between 'specially protected' and 'not specially protected' information is removed, giving all mail information equal protection.
The requirement for employees to be appointed as an 'authorised discloser' to use or disclose information is dropped.
The Bill clarifies that border agency officers and police may open and examine articles when authorised under the Act and other laws.
Provisions allowing handling of articles suspected to contain explosives or dangerous goods are incorporated into the Act.
Terminology for postal offences is updated to match new definitions of when an article is being carried through the mail.
Australian Postal Corporation and Other Legislation Amendment Act 2024
